newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate debt firm, high-yielders fight back.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate debt firm, high-yielders fight back.

text.p: U.S. high-yield debt was in recovery at mid-session after a flurry of early selling took some prices down more than two points, dealers said.
Investment grade debt was firm in thin trade except for some battered cable sector bonds, meanwhile.
Junk-rated gaming sector bonds dominated selling, with highest volume seen in Trump-related debt.

"Several names including Trump had traded off a couple of points but now have traded back up," said a high-yield trader at a big New York shop. "Dealers were long some paper and now the selling has abated and people are buying some bonds."
Trump Atlantic City Funding 11-1/4 percent 10-year first mortgage notes were off their lows at midday but down 3/4 point to 94-3/4 bid, 95-1/4 offer, gaming traders said.
The notes traded as low as 93-3/4 early on Friday.
Trump Castle debt was still down more than one point to 96-1/2 bid, 97 offer compared with a 98 bid on Thursday, another high-yield trader said.

Casino Magic's 11-1/2 percent debt dropped about three points in the fray to trade at 90 before posting a slight recovery. The notes were quoted at 91 bid, 92 offer compared with a 93 bid, 94 offer market late on Thursday.

Stratosphere Corp's 14.25 percent first mortgage notes eroded with the market to 80 bid with no offer, according to two high-yield desks. The notes, bid without accrued interest, were quoted down approximately five points at 82-1/2 bid, 85-1/2 offer late on Thursday.
"There's a bid there but there's nothing much in it," said one high-yield trader. "We haven't seen them trade."

The troubled Las Vegas casino's debt's most recent slide commenced after the hotel/casino said it does not plan to make the November 15 interest payment. The casino also said it will likely file bankruptcy as it restructures terms of the notes.
Grand Casinos Inc owns 42 percent of Stratosphere.
Dealers said movements in gaming was "fairly" reflective of the broad market. High-yield paper was cuffed flat to down 1/8 to 1/4 point and activity was fading fast, traders said.

Turning to high-grade trade, traders reported thin activity but said spreads were attempting to firm outside the cable and media sector. Debt from Tele-Communications Inc eroded for the fifth consecutive session and longer-term paper was close to breaching the 300 basis point spread level, high-grades traders said.
One desk quoted TCI 7-7/8 percent debt due 2026 at 295 basis point bid, 285 offer near mid-session. The debt was quoted near 280 bid by another shop late on Thursday.
Commerce for TCI paper was minimal, traders added.
New issuance was also minimal by mid-session.

Primary action was topped by $250 million 10-year Baa2/BBB-plus rated notes from Mirage Resorts via a Goldman Sachs & Co syndicate. The notes were priced as 7-1/4s at 99.869 to yield 7.268 percent or 73 basis points over the U.S. Treasury curve.
The issue was increased in size by $50 million.
The U.S. Treasury benchmark 30-year bond was trading up 13/32 at 99-4/32 to yield 6.82 percent at 1325 EDT/1725 GMT.
